messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Isolating shape and size
parts:
Nick,

 

Note that Bob’s recommendations were evaluated for univariate response data; though in this case they apply to multivariate data as well.  One option is to account for shape allometry in a phylogenetic context using procD.pgls, rather than procD.lm.  Then, residuals from this analysis have accounted for size, while also taking phylogenetic non-independence into account.

parts:
Hi Dean,

I got the same result when I did it that way. Below is the code I used in geomorph and scatterplot of the correlation between the residuals from procD.lm and procD.pgls. Am I doing something incorrectly with the code here?

Thanks,
Nick

# obtain size-adjusted residuals (and allometry-free shapes)
beak_CS_anova <- procD.lm(two.d.array(shape)~log(size), data = gdf, iter = 999, RRPP=TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)
summary(beak_CS_anova) #same ANOVA Table
shape.resid <- arrayspecs(beak_CS_anova$residuals, p=dim(land)[1], k=dim(land)[2]) #get allometry-adjusted residuals
adj.shape <- shape.resid + array(mshape(land), dim(land)) #get allometry-free shapes

# obtain size-adjusted residuals (and allometry-free shapes while taking into account phylogeny)
beak_CS_phy_anova <- procD.pgls(two.d.array(shape)~log(size), data = gdf, tree, iter = 999, print.progress = TRUE)
summary(beak_CS_phy_anova)
shape.resid.phy <- arrayspecs(beak_CS_phy_anova$residuals, p=dim(land)[1], k=dim(land)[2]) #get allometry-adjusted residuals
adj.shape.phy <- shape.resid.phy + array(mshape(land), dim(shape.resid.phy)) #get allometry-free shapes

plot(beak_CS_anova$residuals ~ beak_CS_phy_anova$residuals)

parts: I found the issue. I was not seeing $pgls.residuals because I was using the formula two.d.array(shape)~log(size). When I used the formula shape~log(size) with procD.pgls, I was able to get $pgls.residuals. Both $residuals and $pgls.residuals were 99% correlated (plot attached). I did a pca on $residuals and $pgls.residuals, the first few axes were nearly perfectly correlated but this relationship started to break down in higher level PCs.

I got the same result when I did it that way. Below is the code I used in geomorph and scatterplot of the correlation between the residuals from procD.lm and procD.pgls. Am I doing something incorrectly with the code here?

Nick

# obtain size-adjusted residuals (and allometry-free shapes)
beak_CS_anova <- procD.lm(two.d.array(shape)~log(size), data = gdf, iter = 999, RRPP=TRUE, print.progress = TRUE)
summary(beak_CS_anova) #same ANOVA Table
shape.resid <- arrayspecs(beak_CS_anova$residuals, p=dim(land)[1], k=dim(land)[2]) #get allometry-adjusted residuals
adj.shape <- shape.resid + array(mshape(land), dim(land)) #get allometry-free shapes

# obtain size-adjusted residuals (and allometry-free shapes while taking into account phylogeny)
beak_CS_phy_anova <- procD.pgls(two.d.array(shape)~log(size), data = gdf, tree, iter = 999, print.progress = TRUE)
summary(beak_CS_phy_anova)
shape.resid.phy <- arrayspecs(beak_CS_phy_anova$residuals, p=dim(land)[1], k=dim(land)[2]) #get allometry-adjusted residuals
adj.shape.phy <- shape.resid.phy + array(mshape(land), dim(shape.resid.phy)) #get allometry-free shapes

plot(beak_CS_anova$residuals ~ beak_CS_phy_anova$residuals)

On Saturday, June 8, 2019 at 11:38:07 AM UTC-7, Adams, Dean [EEOBS] wrote:

Nick,

 

Note that Bob’s recommendations were evaluated for univariate response data; though in this case they apply to multivariate data as well.  One option is to account for shape allometry in a phylogenetic context using procD.pgls, rather than procD.lm.  Then, residuals from this analysis have accounted for size, while also taking phylogenetic non-independence into account.


Dean

I found the issue. I was not seeing $pgls.residuals because I was using the formula two.d.array(shape)~log(size). When I used the formula shape~log(size) with procD.pgls, I was able to get $pgls.residuals. Both $residuals and $pgls.residuals were 99% correlated (plot attached).
